Next: red and purple blood cells with the box Marrow suppression and bullets Thrombocytopenia, Neutropenia. Right: an eye with the box Retinitis and no bullets. There are no axes, numbers, patient names or panel letters.

visual.general_description: Left-to-right management pathway for postnatal CMV from diagnosis criteria through antiviral treatment, monitoring and stopping criteria.
visual.detailed_description: Four chevron-shaped colored headers run left to right on a white background, each above a pale panel of text. Purple header Diagnosis: Severe symptoms as SLS or symptoms in at least 3 of the 5 categories infection, bone marrow suppression, gastrointestinal symptoms, respiratory symptoms, and general appearance; AND; Positive CMV DNA after DOL21 (and negative CMV screening result at birth/before DOL21). Blue header Antiviral treatment: Valganciclovir 16 mg/kg BD PO if tolerating enteral feeds; OR; Ganciclovir 6 mg/kg BD IV, if unable to feed orally. Teal header Monitoring during treatment: FBC, U&E, LFT’s weekly; Blood CMV DNA VL weekly. Green header Discontinue treatment: Treat beyond 2 weeks if symptoms persists and blood VL not fully suppressed; Review every 2 weeks; Rarely treat for more than 4-8 weeks. There are no axes, patient names or panel letters.

visual.general_description: Infographic table comparing six breastmilk treatment techniques by definition, efficacy on CMV eradication and effects on milk elements.
visual.detailed_description: Four-column table-like infographic with column header boxes Technique, Definition, Efficacy on CMV eradication and Effects on BM elements, and six rows. Row 1 Long-Term Pasteurization: thermometer icon, Heating 62.5–63°C for 30 min; virus icon crossed out in red, Complete inactivation. Prevent CMV transmission.; milk-tube icon with a red down arrow, Reduces nutritional, immunological and endocrinological properties. Damages to Ig, lymphocytes, lactoferrin, lysozyme, secretory IgA, bioactive factors, vitamins and hormones. Row 2 Short-Term Pasteurization: Heating 70°C for 5 min OR 72°C for 10 sec OR 62°C for 5 sec; virus icon with a red question-mark icon, Seems promising in CMV inactivation and avoid transmission.; Preserves nutritional and immunological components, enzymes, hormones, growth factors, CMV-specific Ig. Row 3 Freezing: snowflake icon, “Freeze-Thawing: -20°C for a variable time (18h-10 d)”; virus icon with a red down arrow, Reduce viral concentration, without a complete elimination.; Composition, nutritional profile and immunological elements are preserved. But can alter structure of lipids and proteins. Row 4 UV-C Irradiation: UV-C at 200-280 nm for variable time intervals and distance from light; virus icon with red question-mark icon, Seems promising in CMV inactivation. A little viral gene transcription can occur.; red question-mark icon, Beneficial components, such as lactoferrin, lysozyme and secretory IgA seems to be preserved. More studies are needed. Row 5 Microwave Irradiation: High Power (750 W), Low Power (500 W) for 30 sec; virus icon with red question-mark icon, Seems promising in CMV inactivation. High Power: complete eradication. Low Power: failure rate of 13%.; red question-mark icon and small down arrow, Few studies about its effects on immunological, bioactive, cellular and nutritive components. It seems to induce a little decrease in Ig concentration, without altering the fatty acids’ composition. Row 6 Others: bulleted list High pressure processing, Thermo-ultrasonication, Retort processing, “Pulsed electric field treatme” (printed text cut off at the box edge), Gamma irradiation, Microfiltration; virus icon with red question-mark icon, More studies are needed to evaluate effects on CMV transmission.; red question-mark icon, More studies are needed to understand nutritional and bioactive effects on BM. No patient data are shown.

visual.general_description: Map infographic of national and European recommendations on fresh, frozen or pasteurized breastmilk for infants of CMV-positive mothers.
visual.detailed_description: A pale blue world map on a white background with nine beige rounded boxes, each with a country or region name, flag icon, dated recommendation text and the issuing society in parentheses; thin black lines connect each box to a point on the map in Europe or the United States. SPAIN: 2011 : Freezing BM for premature babies LBW after 7 DOL when mother is CMV-positive (Spanish group for Paediatric Infectious Diseases - SEIP). FRANCE: 2005 : Pasteurization of BM for premature babies <32 wks or <1500 gr if mother is CMV-positive (French Society for the Safety of Nutrition); 2018: Pasteurization of BM when CMV-IgG is positive or unknown for babies born <28 wks or <1000 gr after 3 DOL up to 31+6 weeks (French Neonatal Society’s working group on fresh human milk use in preterm infants). SWEDEN: 2011: Consider freezing BM for very immature neonates (Swedish Neonatal Association). POLAND: 2021 : Fresh BM recommended (Polish Society of Neonatology). USA: 2012 : Fresh BM recommended; 2024: When available, pasteurization for BM <32 wks of GA, if the mother is CMV-positive (American Academy of Pediatrics - AAP). GERMANY: 2023: Pasteurization of BM <32 wks if mother CMV-positive (German Federal Association “The premature Baby”). EUROPE: 2022 : Fresh BM recommended (ESPGHAN). ITALY: 2015 : Fresh BM recommended (SIP, SIN, SICuPP, SIGENP). AUSTRIA: Pasteurization of BM if mother is CMV-positive for babies born <28 wks or <1000 gr after 3 DOL up to 32+0 weeks (Committee for Nutrition of the Austrian Society of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine). There are no axes, patient names or panel letters.
